newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana Energy raises oil, gas reserves.
newsitem.headline: Wascana Energy raises oil, gas reserves.

text.p: Wascana Energy Inc released higher oil and gas reserve estimates on Sunday as the Regina-based company seeks to fend off a hostile C$1.7 billion takeover bid by Talisman Energy Inc.
The updated reserve estimates resulted from new exploration and drilling, seismec work and an independent evaluation, Wascana said in a statement.
Wascana estimated it now has a total of 236 million proven barrels of oil equivalent (BOE), 29 percent more than reported in the company's 1996 results.
It also estimated proven and probable BOEs at 303 million, 24 percent higher than previously reported.
Proven oil is up 37 million barrels, or 27.4 percent, and proven gas is up 155 billion cubic feet, or 32.3 percent, Wascana said.
"These new numbers bode well for the future of Wascana shareholders," Wascana chief executive Frank Proto said in the statement.
Last week, Proto said interest from potential rival bidders was strong. Wascana opened data rooms in Calgary last week while its board of directors reviewed Talisman's offer.
Calgary-based Talisman is offering C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share.
Wascana's new reserve calculation was conducted by Ryder Scott Co, a U.S.-based oil and gas evaluation firm.
Forty-five million proven BOEs come from new discoveries and incremental development and 7.4 million proven BOEs come from improved property performance and other changes, Wascana said.

"The Smiley-Buffalo field near Lloydminster has become the second largest pool to be discovered in Saskatchewan in the last ten years, and has proved to be a much more significant heavy oil find than was first projected," Proto said.

The Smiley-Buffalo field, discovered by Wascana in north central Saskatchewan, has 17.3 million barrels of proven reserves, and Wascana's South Winter pool has been assigned 2.9 million barrels of proven reserves.

The reserves booked by Ryder Scott resulted from strong first-quarter 1997 drilling, 3D seismic interpretation, drilling programs that have identified further development opportunities, and some evaluation differences based on production experience, Wascana said.
